title: LLMResolvedDataEdges (Scala)

LLMResolvedEdge.description:
One data edge produced by the LLM data-edge resolution pass.

Stored in :class:`LLMResolvedDataEdges` and consumed by
``render_assessment --llm-resolved-edges`` to augment the data DAG.

Language-neutral: applies to ``.scala`` (and any ``.sql`` / ``.ipynb``
in the same workload).

file.description: Workload-relative path of the file containing the call.
file.title: File

line.description:
Source line of the read/write call.  For a ``resolved_unresolved`` edge
this MUST equal the ``line`` of the matching ``unresolved_data_edges``
entry so the reconciliation gate can pair them.
line.title: Line

kind.description:
The I/O verb: ``read`` / ``write`` most commonly, but the LLM also emits
``merge`` / ``delete`` / ``drop`` / ``truncate`` when the source uses them.
:func:`edge_lineage_role` maps each verb to source / sink / neutral for
edge building — destructive verbs (``drop`` / ``delete`` / ``truncate``) are
neutral and never create writer→reader edges.  Kept as a free string
(not a strict enum) so an unforeseen verb degrades to a logged warning
rather than failing IR validation and silently dropping all LLM data.
kind.title: Kind

resolved_signature.description: Normalised path/table/bucket signature, ready for the data DAG.
resolved_signature.title: Resolved Signature

resolution_type.description:
Confidence of the resolution.  All three levels are drawn in the DAG;
the level is kept for audit / optional filtering.
resolution_type.title: Resolution Type

explanation.description: Human-readable derivation chain — populated for audit, not rendering.
explanation.title: Explanation

source.description:
See :data:`EdgeSource`.  Required — a missing/typo'd value used to
silently break reconciliation, so it is now a validated enum.
source.title: Source

LLMResolvedEdge.title: LLMResolvedEdge

LLMUnresolvableEdge.description:
A read/write call site the LLM read and confirmed is unresolvable.

Replaces the former untyped ``list[dict]`` so ``line``/``kind`` are
guaranteed present (they render as table columns AND key the
reconciliation gate — an entry missing either silently failed to suppress
its matching ``unresolved_data_edges`` row).

file.description:
Workload-relative path.  Must match the ``unresolved_data_edges`` entry
this confirms, so the renderer can move the row out of the plain
'unresolved' table into the 'confirmed unresolvable' table.
file.title: File

why_unresolvable.description:
Clear reason: dead code, pure runtime value, delegated to a SQL node,
stale reference outside the workload, etc.
why_unresolvable.title: Why Unresolvable

LLMUnresolvableEdge.title: LLMUnresolvableEdge

OrchestrationEdge.description:
A pipeline-ordering / handoff relationship between two workload files.

Data-signature matching links a *writer* file to a *reader* file only when
they share a table/path.  But pipeline stages are often chained by control
or parameter handoffs that share NO table — a Databricks Scala notebook's
``dbutils.jobs.taskValues.set`` in one cell read by ``taskValues.get`` in the
next, a ``%run`` include, an external job-dependency edge, an SBT task
dependency, or a method-call chain across Scala objects in a single JVM
process.  The LLM understands the pipeline order (it writes the advisory),
so it records those handoffs here; the renderer draws them as dashed
``orchestrates`` arrows so an orchestrator stage is never left an isolated
island.

from_file.description: Workload-relative path of the upstream / orchestrating stage.
from_file.title: From File

to_file.description: Workload-relative path of the downstream stage it hands off to.
to_file.title: To File

mechanism.description:
How the handoff happens. Scala/Databricks mechanisms:
``dbutils.taskValues``, ``%run``, ``job_dependency``, ``notebook_workflow``
(Databricks notebook orchestration); ``sbt_task_dependency`` (SBT multi-
module build); ``method_call_chain`` (objects in one JVM process); or a free
string for an unforeseen mechanism. Shown in the tooltip.
mechanism.title: Mechanism

explanation.description:
One line on how this was determined (e.g. which task-value keys, which
SBT project depends-on, which object method is called).
explanation.title: Explanation

OrchestrationEdge.title: OrchestrationEdge

description:
Container for all LLM data-edge resolution output stored in the IR
for a Scala workload.

Written by the Scala ``data_edge_resolver`` agent (see
``agents/data_edge_resolver.md``) and read by
``render_assessment --llm-resolved-edges --language scala``.

NOTE: unlike the Python schema, this Scala variant has NO
``resolved_imports`` field — Scala imports are compile-time (resolved by the
compiler / Scalameta), so there is no dynamic-import resolution pass.

edges.description:
All data edges produced by the LLM — both resolved-unresolved and
newly-discovered.  All resolution types (``literal_found`` / ``traced`` /
``inferred``) are drawn in the DAG; ``resolution_type`` records confidence.
edges.title: Edges

analyzed_files.description:
Workload-relative paths of every file the LLM read and found to have
data I/O.  Every path that appears in ``edges`` must also appear here.
Together with ``excluded_files`` these must cover every
``.scala`` / ``.sql`` / ``.ipynb`` in the workload — the gate checks this.
analyzed_files.title: Analyzed Files

excluded_files.description:
Workload-relative paths of every file the LLM read and confirmed has
NO data I/O (pure utility code, init files, test stubs, etc.).
excluded_files.title: Excluded Files

unresolvable_edges.description:
Read/write edges the LLM confirmed are runtime-only or otherwise
structurally unresolvable.  Their ``(file, line, kind)`` keys move the
matching ``unresolved_data_edges`` rows into the audited 'confirmed
unresolvable' table.
unresolvable_edges.title: Unresolvable Edges

orchestration_edges.description:
Pipeline-ordering handoffs between files that share no table (task
values, ``%run``, job dependencies, SBT task deps, method-call chains).
Drawn as dashed ``orchestrates`` arrows so orchestrator stages join the DAG
instead of rendering as isolated islands.
orchestration_edges.title: Orchestration Edges

llm_insights.description:
Short advisory bullets (one sentence each) the LLM agent writes after
analysing all unresolvable edges — e.g. missing orchestration files,
dead-code patterns, incomplete workload exports.  Rendered in the HTML
report as an "Advisory — what this means" callout.
llm_insights.title: Llm Insights
